title: Hipparcos (1990-1993) and TESS (2018-2026) eclipse depths agree for most of 79 bright detached binaries; the one large depth change, in HD 35104, comes from apsidal motion with a period near 80 years
abstract: Campaign studies found rare eclipse-depth changes caused by a turning orbital plane (HD 93683, HD 303514), mostly from ASAS-3 and TESS in the south. We added an all-sky epoch 30 years older. We fitted TESS 2-min eclipse templates of 849 eclipsing binaries of the Prsa et al. (2022) catalogue to their Hipparcos epoch photometry (1989.9-1993.2). The fit gives the depth ratio k = depth(Hipparcos)/depth(TESS) with the eclipse time free inside the ephemeris error. For the 79 usable binaries that are single stars in Hipparcos, k has a median of 1.02 and a 16-84 percent range of 0.87-1.07. The method recovers the known eclipse loss of HS Hya (k > 29). Seven binaries pass a rule for much shallower eclipses in 1990-1993 and none for much deeper eclipses. Four are Hipparcos double-star solutions, two (LO Hya, V1200 Cen) have full-depth eclipses 0.22 d away from the TESS ephemeris (timing changes), and one, HD 35104 (B8, P = 1.664 d), has a real change: a primary depth of 2.8 +- 0.7 percent in 1990-1993 against 8.2-8.6 percent in TESS. In TESS its secondary eclipse moved from phase 0.542 (2018.9) to 0.484 (2026.6). An eccentric two-star model with apsidal motion and constant inclination, fitted to TESS only, gives e = 0.16 and an apsidal period of 86 yr and predicts a 1991 primary depth of 3.8 percent; joint fits give 74-78 yr. In all fits the primary-conjunction impact parameter was 0.75-0.78 of the radius sum in 1991 and is 0.56-0.60 now, so apsidal motion, not a turning plane, explains the change. Tycho and Kepler show that Hipparcos epoch magnitudes of the 1.2-arcsec pair HIP 93954 miss its eclipses, so double-star solutions must be excluded. Thus no testable single-star binary shows a factor-2 depth change from nodal precession (95 percent upper limit 3.7 percent). Limits: 79 testable systems, band differences between Hp and TESS, a spherical-star model with residuals 17.5 times the photon noise, and no spectroscopy.
